title: simple-dispatcher: every Stop outcome posts its relays through one sequence
description:
Repo: JKershaw/simple-dispatcher

## Goal

Every way a session's Stop hook can end posts its relays through **one sequence**, so that adding or changing a relay is one edit, and no outcome can be missed.

## Why now

Today each case of `hook.js`'s Stop switch carries its own relay calls (ticket markers, tool activity, usage, text and status), in orders defended by comments. That has had a real cost:

* one shipped miss: tool activity was wired into 3 of 6 outcomes, and a second ticket was needed for the rest;
* a hand-check of every exit path on each relay ticket, about five times in four months;
* one place where new work went around the switch rather than into it.

Three Surveys named this as the right direction but not their task's to carry (LIN-4165, LIN-4183, LIN-4203; see `docs/plans/survey/broad-options.md` on branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j` of LinearViewer). A pricing follow-up on LIN-4203 put it here, on its own and after LIN-4203: the snapshot removal makes every tail one call shorter, and mixing this refactor with a behaviour change would hide which one moved a post.

**Sequenced after LIN-4203** (stop posting usage snapshots). Don't start before it merges.

## Done when

* For every Stop outcome, the ordered posts and cursor commits are what they were before. That is shown by a characterization recording made **before** any refactor, checked with each relay flag on and off, and shown to fail when one post is moved.
* The outcomes that really do differ (where status comes last, posting before a hold, the case that posts nothing) are named in one place, not spread across cases.
* Adding a relay is one change in one place.

## Report back

What changed · what was left, and why · what still looks fuzzy · follow-ups, listed rather than filed.

---

*Filed by [Claude Code](<https://claude.ai/code>) for the Survey research*

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Two Surveys at simple-dispatcher `d8d186c` (on LIN-4150) agree on where this binds:

* **There's no single order to extract: three real shapes plus exceptions.** Status first (block, self-check, zero-tool). "statusLast" (defer, blocked, failed). And complete, where the marker moves to just before `[done]`. Refused block and allow post nothing. Text is turn-final in some cases and additive in others.
* **Decision/withdraw is written out three times** (self-check, blocked, complete), and `betweenTextAndStatus` is a fourth way in. Leave those at the call sites and the sequence becomes a second home beside the old one.
* **Cursor commits don't show in** `posts`**.** Snapshot state inside the `respond` callback on each POST, so each post carries its cursor state.
* **Flags are fixed at require time,** so each combination needs a cold reload (`fresh-config.js` already does this). The hold paths and the failed-`[done]` path need their own rows.
* **A latent bug the refactor must not hide:** with `SD_TOOL_ACTIVITY_RELAY=1`, defer, blocked and failed post tool activity *after* their status, so Harbour's `parseParkedWait` misses the park. **Preserve it here and name it as an exception in the table.** The fix is LIN-4233, after this.

### Scope decision (4 Nov, about 18:45 UTC)

John asked Claude to take the human's role in this process and choose a large enough option. **The decision: one table of outcome orders plus one executor, with decision/withdraw folded in as a slot and the usage flush as slot 0.** In pieces, golden first:

1. **The characterization golden, on its own.** A table-driven test over outcome × flag set (`TEXT`, `MARKER`, `TOOL` on and off, plus the hold and failed-`[done]` paths), recording `(kind, message head, cursor snapshot)` per POST and then the stdout decision. **Prove it's sensitive:** move one post (e.g. A before S in defer) and watch it fail.
2. **The table and executor.** Each outcome maps to its ordered slots. The exceptions are declared in that one place: status-first, status-last-with-trailing-tool (named, with LIN-4233), the late marker in complete, post-before-hold, and post-nothing. **Decision/withdraw becomes a slot; its three copies and** `betweenTextAndStatus` **are deleted.**
3. **The usage flush as slot 0**, with the refused block modelled, so "every relay in one place" is true.

**At merge (we'll check it):**

* the golden is unchanged for every row;
* no relay post call remains inside the switch cases;
* one table names every outcome's order and exceptions;
* `betweenTextAndStatus` and the copied decision blocks are gone;
* the stale comments at `hook.js:2171` and opencode-runner's stale `hook.js` citations are corrected (not merged).

**Not this task's:** the park-status fix (LIN-4233); decision scanning in outcomes that never do it today; sharing the sequence with `opencode-runner.js`; splitting `main()`'s effects.

## Implementation Plan

**Session fit:** fits one session
**plan-review due: no**

*Pruned at close-out (4 Nov 2026).* The plan was implemented as approved: one `STOP_OUTCOMES` table plus one executor (`runStopOutcome`) in `hook.js`, built golden-first in three commits (golden, table + executor, usage flush as slot 0). Merged in [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/325](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/325>) as `bf499a4`. One deviation from the plan, made at close-out on review's finding: `defer` reads `deferredAt` inside its `prepare` so it is stamped after the slot-0 flush (`055f8e8`). The park-status quirk stays as the `statusLastTrailingTool` exception (LIN-4233). The full pre-prune description is preserved in the task snapshots, and the plan's detail and the review are in the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Unblock check: LIN-4218 is unblocked

**The blocker is cleared.** LIN-4203 is **Done**. Runner PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/323 merged at 17:18Z as `44ab30e`, and Harbour PR #2274 merged as `d7ceb373`. No other blocker exists, so there was nothing for a person to decide and no full blocker analysis to do.

**What it costs to wait:** while this sits, every new relay ticket still needs someone to check each Stop exit by hand. LIN-4233 (the park-status fix) is also held up, because it is sequenced after this ticket.

**Recorded:**
- Relation **LIN-4203 blocks LIN-4218**. The dependency was only written in the description before.
- Relation **LIN-4218 blocks LIN-4233**, as the description says ("the fix is LIN-4233, after this").
- Status: Todo → In Progress.

### Checked against the code at `origin/main` `d8d186c`
Since this ticket was filed (11:06Z), only one commit has touched `hook.js` or `opencode-runner.js`: `44ab30e`, which is LIN-4203 itself. So the description's shape still holds. Corrections for whoever builds this:
- The stale comment cited as `hook.js:2171` is now at **`hook.js:2172`**, in the complete branch's decision block (from about line 2170).
- `betweenTextAndStatus` is defined in `feedbackWithText` at `hook.js:438-445`. Its call site is the blocked path at about `hook.js:2040-2069`.
- The usage flush that will become slot 0 is `flushRequestUsageSafely` at about `hook.js:1824-1827`.
- The cold-reload helper is `test/helpers/fresh-config.js` (`loadFresh`, `driveStopHook`), not `test/fresh-config.js`.
- opencode-runner's citations of `hook.js` lines: `:17` is still correct. **`:262` (line 362), `:944-946` (line 956) and `:716/854` (line 1284) are stale.** They now point at unrelated code, so they need fixing as part of this ticket's at-merge list.
- LIN-4233 is in Backlog, which is consistent with keeping the tool-after-status quirk here.

### Next action
Dispatch the **build** for LIN-4218 as the description lays it out, golden first:
1. The characterization golden, in a PR or commit of its own, with the sensitivity check (move A before S in defer and watch it fail).
2. The table plus one executor, with decision/withdraw as a slot.
3. The usage flush as slot 0.

I didn't start the build in this session. The dispatch was to unblock the ticket, and the build is a large, golden-first refactor that should run as its own dispatch. I don't hold the `dispatch` grant, so the orchestrator needs to queue it.

## LIN-4218: PR open, CI green

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/325 (branch `feat/lin-4218-stop-relay-order`, 3 commits: golden `18b8527`, table + executor `aecb8b0`, flush as slot 0 `34457f5`).

**What changed:** every relay a Stop posts is one row of `STOP_OUTCOMES` in `hook.js`, walked by `runStopOutcome`. The Stop switch keeps only each case's own commits, stdout and non-relay effects. The decision/withdraw scan is one slot, so `betweenTextAndStatus` and the three copies are gone. Exceptions are named once, in the table's comment. `docs/module-map.md` names the table.

**Evidence:**
- Characterization golden (20 scenarios × 8 relay-flag sets, every POST and stdout, cursor state at each POST) recorded before the refactor. It passes unchanged after it.
- Golden is shown to fail on planted moves: defer tool-before-status (12 rows), block marker-after-status (4 rows), blocked decision-after-status (16 rows), flush moved after the block commit (block-refused).
- `npm test`: 4249 tests, 4244 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (baseline 4239 / 4234 / 0 / 5).
- Mutation gate `npm run test:mutation`: 67/67 killed.
- CI (`unit tests`): pass, 2m59s.

**Not done / caveats:**
- Harbour system suite (`npm run test:system`) not run here; CI does not run it.
- Blocked "not held" is unreachable from `decideHookAction` (blocked is always holdable), so the golden covers only the held path.
- LIN-4233 (park status last with tool activity on) is preserved as the `statusLastTrailingTool` exception, not fixed.
- Ready for review; merge is for the reviewer/orchestrator.

## Review — LIN-4218

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/325, reviewed at head `34457f5` (commits `18b8527` golden → `aecb8b0` table + executor → `34457f5` flush as slot 0), base `origin/main` `d8d186c`.

CI: green. `unit tests` passed on `34457f5` (run 41890271212). I also re-ran these myself: `npm test` on the PR gave 4249 / 4244 pass / 0 fail / 5 skip, and base gave 4239 / 4234 / 0 / 5, with the same failure names (none). `npm run test:system` against Harbour `d7ceb373` gave **127/127 pass**. The PR had left that one not run, so that caveat is now discharged.

### Scope vs plan
The PR matches the plan's places and three-commit order. Only `hook.js`, `opencode-runner.js` (comment edits), `docs/module-map.md`, the mutation-gate find string and tests changed. Nothing went beyond the plan. Staleness: no commit has touched `hook.js`, `opencode-runner.js` or `test/helpers/fresh-config.js` on main since the ticket was filed, apart from `44ab30e` (LIN-4203), which the plan already accounts for.

### At-merge list, checked
- **Golden unchanged for every row.** `git diff 18b8527 34457f5` on the golden and its test is empty. **Independent replay:** I ran the PR's golden test against `origin/main`'s unchanged `hook.js` and it passed 2/2. So the golden is a real recording of pre-refactor behaviour, not something fitted to the new code.
- **No relay post inside the switch.** I found no relay or `feedback(` call anywhere in `main()` outside `runStopOutcome`.
- **One table names every outcome's order and exceptions.** `STOP_OUTCOMES` has all 8 rows. Its slot orders match the plan's table exactly, including the `statusLastTrailingTool` exception that cites LIN-4233.
- **`betweenTextAndStatus`, `feedbackWithText` and the 3 decision copies are gone.** They are replaced by `relayDecisionAndWithdrawals`. The `feedback-metadata` cases were re-pointed at the table rather than dropped.
- **Stale comments.** `hook.js` and `opencode-runner.js` now cite symbols, not line numbers.

### Mutation check (mine; every mutation reverted, worktree clean)
Each mutation below made the named test fail:

| Mutation | What failed |
|---|---|
| `failed`: A before S | golden, 4 rows (`failed\|*A1`) and the exceptions check |
| `self-check`: D after S | golden, 8 rows |
| `complete`: M after S (lateMarker broken) | golden, 20 rows and the exceptions check |
| `complete`: E before A | golden, 4 rows |
| `defer`: U dropped | the usage-record precondition and the "U is slot 0" check |
| `zero-tool-challenge`: text `additive` → `final` | golden, 4 rows (flag-off) |
| executor stops returning `statusResult` | golden, 32 complete rows (the failed-`[done]` path) |
| `blocked`: `statusExtra` (issueLink / refusal) dropped | golden, 8 `blocked-refusal` rows |
| a planted `postTicketMarkerDelta(` call in the `failed` case | the census |

The author's own runs (defer A before S, block M after S, blocked D after S, flush after C) are in the PR body. I did not repeat them.

### Regression check
`git log -30` on `hook.js` and `opencode-runner.js` shows two fixes this change must keep:
- **LIN-3437** (abort wins and a block is refused): still covered, by the `block-refused` row with an abort during the flush.
- **LIN-4165** (duplicate assistant text): `relayAssistantText` is untouched.

No recent revert is being re-applied.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is relay posts on the Stop path. Inside `hook.js`, every instance now goes through the table. The siblings outside it are the ones the ticket already excludes:
- `reapers.js`'s heartbeat marker emitter is another process.
- `opencode-runner.js` orders posts by beat and was ruled out.
- `holdAndMaybeInject`'s post-hold resume entry is a hold effect, which the plan keeps in the cases.

No unhandled sibling falls inside the ticket's bounded classes.

### Findings
1. **Minor; close-out fix.** Commit 3 moved the flush from before the switch into slot 0 of each row. As a result, two clock reads that used to happen after the flush now happen before it:
   - In `case 'defer'`, `const deferredAt = Date.now()` is committed as `live.deferredAt`, the stall selectors' fallback clock. It is now earlier by the flush time (at most `REQUEST_USAGE_FLUSH_BUDGET_MS`, 5s by default).
   - In `case 'complete'`, `duration` (the `[done] Task completed in …` text) is now computed before the flush.

   The golden can't see this, because it normalises every epoch value to `<ts>`. Plan decision 4 ("the flush still runs before every case-specific commit") covers the committed value in spirit. **Fix:** in `hook.js` `case 'defer'`, move `const deferredAt = Date.now();` inside the `prepare` callback, just before its `commit(...)`. `deferredAt` is used only in that commit. Leaving `duration` as it is is fine: it is display text and the shift is seconds. Note it in the PR as deliberate.
2. **Disclosed in the PR; acceptable.** The oplog lines `decision.suppressed` and `withdraw.suppressed` now come after T/S instead of before M. The plan says oplog order is not a contract, and `test/decision-suppression.test.js` passes.
3. **Disclosed in the PR; acceptable.** Blocked "not held" can't be reached from `decideHookAction`, so the golden doesn't cover it. That is a limit of the golden, not a gap in the code: the case has no relay logic of its own, and the shared `blocked` row is covered.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (bounded class: "the flush still runs before every case-specific commit", plan decision 4): `defer`'s committed `deferredAt` should be read after the U slot. Today the golden normalises timestamps, so it passes either way. **Before the merge:** close-out makes the finding 1 fix, then re-runs the golden and `npm test`. The test that tells right from wrong: with a stubbed slow flush (for example, `flushRequestUsageSafely` resolving after 1s), the committed `deferredAt` must be ≥ the time the flush resolved. Code inspection after the move is also enough, because `deferredAt` then has no read before `prepare`.
- **Inside** (one table names every outcome; table-coverage test): an unknown future `action.type` gets the allow row, with no flush. Before this PR, any non-`allow` type got the flush. Today no such type can be reached: `stop-relay-table.test.js` checks that every type `decideHookActionInner` returns has a row. **Discharged** by that test, so nothing is left for close-out.
- **Outside**: the LIN-4233 park-status-after-tool quirk is deliberately kept. It is already filed and blocked by this ticket, so no new ticket is needed.

### Verdict
`Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger`

The refactor is complete, and against the at-merge list. The golden is proven both pre-refactor and sensitive, and CI, the system suite and the base/PR suite comparison are all green. Close-out should move `deferredAt` into `defer`'s `prepare`, re-run the golden and `npm test`, then merge.

## Close-out — LIN-4218

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/325 → `main` as squash `bf499a4`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 055f8e8` (the commit CI passed on). The deployed checkout (`/Users/autopilot/development/simple-dispatcher`) is at `bf499a4`.

Every Stop outcome now posts its relays through one `STOP_OUTCOMES` table walked by `runStopOutcome` in `hook.js`. The usage flush is slot 0 of every non-`allow` row. The decision/withdraw scan is one slot. `betweenTextAndStatus` and `feedbackWithText` are gone. The exceptions are named once, in the table's comment.

### Changes I made after the approval
| Commit | Review line it answers |
|---|---|
| `055f8e8` (`hook.js` `case 'defer'` + new `test/defer-deferred-at-after-flush.test.js`) | Finding 1: `deferredAt = Date.now()` moved into `defer`'s `prepare`, just before its commit, so it is read after the slot-0 flush. `duration` in complete's `[done]` text is left before the flush on purpose, as review allowed (display text, a shift of seconds). |

No stale citation or comment came out of this change.

### Ledger
- **Inside: `deferredAt` read after the flush.** Fixed in `055f8e8`. Witness: the new test stubs `flushRequestUsageSafely` to resolve after 150ms and asserts the committed `deferredAt` ≥ the moment the flush resolved. It **fails on `34457f5`** (`deferredAt (…002) must not predate the flush resolving (…155)`) and passes on `055f8e8`. After the move `deferredAt` has no read before `prepare`.
- **Inside: unknown future `action.type` gets the allow row, no flush.** Discharged by review through `stop-relay-table.test.js`; nothing left for close-out.
- **Outside: LIN-4233** (park status after tool activity). Already filed and Backlog. It was blocked by this ticket and is now unblocked. No new ticket and no new relation needed.
- No named monitor or rollback was recorded in the ledger, and none is claimed.

### CI and checks
- CI exists (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). `unit tests` passed on `055f8e8` in 2m57s (run 41892525822, `headSha` = `055f8e8`, read before the merge).
- Local, before the push: golden + table tests 10/10; `npm test` 4250 tests, 4245 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (the PR's 4249 plus the new test); `npm run test:mutation` 67/67 killed.
- Review's own run: `npm run test:system` 127/127 against Harbour `d7ceb373`. I did not re-run it, because the change since is a one-line clock-read move in the `defer` case.

### After the merge
No post-deploy step was named in the ledger. On merged `main` at `bf499a4` I re-ran the golden, table and new test files: 11/11 pass.

### Follow-ups
None filed. The only outside item is already LIN-4233.

### Description
Archived with a snapshot first, then pruned. The plan sections are replaced by a stub, and the full history is in the task snapshots and this comment trail.
